title: postgresql.conf Memory & Cache Tuning
description: Tune shared_buffers, work_mem, maintenance_work_mem, effective_cache_size, and max_wal_size for production servers.

data.text: Default PostgreSQL configuration settings are deliberately conservative so the engine can boot on constrained hardware. Tuning memory parameters for your server's RAM profile unlocks significant performance gains.

rows: Primary in-memory data page cache for tables and indexes.
Planner assumption of available memory (PostgreSQL shared buffers + Linux OS page cache).
Memory allocated for each sort, hash, and join operation per query.
Memory used for VACUUM, CREATE INDEX, and ALTER TABLE migrations.
Controls checkpoint frequency; larger values reduce disk write spikes.

data.title: Caution with work_mem
data.text: `work_mem` is allocated per query operation, NOT per connection! A complex query with 4 joins and 2 sorts can allocate 6 × work_mem. Setting `work_mem = 1GB` globally with 100 connections can cause the Linux kernel Out-Of-Memory (OOM) killer to crash the database.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Tune `work_mem` carefully to avoid OOM crashes during concurrent joins and sorts.
Increase `maintenance_work_mem` to accelerate index creation and autovacuum.
